scenes.tts: Wöhler's critics had an escape route: his ammonium cyanate could be traced back to organic sources, so perhaps no organic molecule had truly been made from the lifeless world. Kolbe's 1845 synthesis slammed that door.
scenes.visual: Wöhler's critics' escape route; Kolbe 1845 slams the door
scenes.narration: Wöhler's critics had an escape route: his ammonium cyanate could be traced back to organic sources, so perhaps no organic molecule had truly been made from the lifeless world. Kolbe's 1845 synthesis slammed that door.

scenes.tts: He started from carbon disulfide — made from charcoal and molten sulfur, with nothing alive anywhere in the chain — and finished the job not with a cell or a seed but with an ordinary galvanic battery, leaving pure acetic acid behind.
scenes.visual: carbon disulfide from charcoal+sulfur; battery; acetic acid

scenes.tts: Whatever his own motive (he was chiefly proving a theory of how molecules are built), the effect was decisive: no organic source remained to point to.

scenes.tts: That two-carbon acetyl group is now the most-trafficked fragment in all of metabolism.
